A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BISE research and contain the complete main paper and Appendices A–N. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original BISE experiments across five benchmarks, together with ablations, sensitivity studies, and robustness analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark results and supplementary experimental analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same structured pruning masks, frozen model parameters, reweighted classification loss, auxiliary bias classifier, mutual-information regularization, and optional finetuning.

E1.justification: Both versions use BiasedMNIST, Corrupted-CIFAR10, CelebA, Multi-Color MNIST, and CivilComments. The unsupervised, extreme-bias, and noisy-label scenarios in the main text and appendices are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the reported comparisons, including FFW in Table 7 and Appendices F/G, and random and magnitude pruning in Figure 3b.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.4 and Appendices C–M retain the same data configurations, architectures, training budgets, validation-based selection procedures, evaluation metrics, and supplementary experimental protocols.

E4.justification: The loss ablation and pruning comparisons in Section 4.3 are retained. The appendix studies of hyperparameters, batch normalization, pruning thresholds, noisy bias labels, and bias information in representations are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging across three seeds, retain the three-best-seeds statement for unsupervised CelebA, and use the same uncertainty reporting, including standard-deviation shading in Figure 3.

E6.justification: Numerical results and plotted findings match throughout the main paper and appendices. For example, BISE remains at 96.1 ± 0.5% in Table 1 for rho = 0.99 and 15.7 ± 1.3% in Table G.1 for rho = 0.999; no result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and objectives in Section 3, mutual-information assumptions and derivations in Appendix A, and reweighting derivations in Appendix B are unchanged. Minor index typography does not change the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about extracting bias-resistant subnetworks without altering the original weights or requiring additional unbiased training data, with optional finetuning improving performance.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same interpretations and limitations, including difficulties with interacting biases, dependence on an unbiased subnetwork already existing, and the severe-bias failure discussion in Appendix G.

D1.justification: The implementation and reproducibility information is unchanged, including PyTorch version, GPU hardware, optimizer settings, training schedules, masking details, and the code-access disclosure.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 111 works and retain the same research positioning. Reference edits concern formatting and venue metadata, such as changing reference 79 from CVPR to CVPR Workshops, rather than adding or removing research.

P1.justification: v2 removes Genoa from the third affiliation, gives the acknowledgments a standalone heading, adds ELIAS/Horizon Europe funding acknowledgment, and makes bibliographic style edits. The scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded acknowledgments cause reference-page reflow. Small display edits include changing sample indices from i to j in Figure 2 and standardizing the BISE asterisk in Table N.1; no figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 adds funding acknowledgment and makes limited bibliographic, notation, and layout edits. The method, experimental evidence, mathematical reasoning, and limitations remain unchanged throughout the main paper and appendices, leaving overall paper quality essentially stable.
